The booklet is 27 pages: idx 0 is the bilingual cover (Series S3RQP, SET-2, Q.P. Code 57/3/2, BIOLOGY (Theory), 3 hours, 70 marks; last folio 'Page 27 of 27'); idx 1 is the Hindi instructions; every ODD index 3-25 is the Hindi facing page (checked on the contact sheet and by the text layer, where no odd page carries any English word of five letters or more beyond the running header), so no English overflows onto an odd page and the parity never inverts. idx 26 is the last page and is English (Q33(b)). Born-digital: the text layer was used as a DRAFT only and every row was checked against the full-size page. FOLLOWER of 57/3/1: every question that matches the opener was confirmed on this paper's own page and its stem, context, options, chapter, subtopic and _drawFigure reused byte for byte; every _figure note was written from this paper's own pages (the gel diagram, bar graph and nicotine graph were compared side by side with the opener's pages and are the same drawings). Instruction (viii) names Sections B, D and E but gives no count; the roster was built from the marking scheme's bare ORs and confirmed against a printed OR on the page: Q17, Q18, Q20, Q29(c), Q30(a), Q31, Q32, Q33, eight alternatives, none in Section C. Primary marks: A16 + B10 + C21 + D8 + E15 = 70. Section-A key read off the scheme IMAGE (ms idx 2) and independently from the scheme's text layer: DBDBCCBDCAAAAACC, 16 of 16 agree. No CBSE void anywhere in the scheme (every page read; no award-regardless, misprint, Hindi-medium or either-of-two note). Q29's passage prints raised dots (8·1, 2·4). Quotes straight, scientific names and Latin phrases plain text (the Biology rules).

questions.context:
India is one of the megadiverse countries housing around \(8{\cdot}1\) per cent of global species diversity, although its land area is only \(2{\cdot}4\) per cent of the world's land area. Many of the species are highly threatened due to human activities like deforestation, mining and habitat fragmentation. Laws like Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 were enacted by the Government of India to preserve our biological wealth. Various conservation measures are being implemented to save the threatened species.
The following bar graph shows the number of species conserved under different biodiversity conservation methods.
Study the graph and answer the questions.
questions.stem: Which method conserves the highest number of species ? Is it ex situ or in situ conservation ?
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a bar graph titled 'Species Conserved under Different Biodiversity Conservation Methods', Number of Species Conserved (0 to 3000) against Conservation Method, five bars each with its count printed above it. The method named under each bar and the counts decide (a), so they are withheld here. Same drawing as 57/3/1 Q30 (compared side by side). Page idx 18.
